picks.why: Talen is the cheapest way on the shortlist into the power-bottleneck thesis: about 12x forward earnings, revenue up 111%, a 7% free-cash-flow yield and 19% below its high. It sells power from existing plants, so it gains from the constraint without the build risk of pre-revenue nuclear.
picks.risk: Its operating margin is negative on the latest numbers, so the cash flow may rest on one-off items rather than the core business.

picks.why: SanDisk trades near 5x forward earnings with 78% operating margins and revenue up 372%, yet sits 41% below its high. It is the most discounted large memory name if the supercycle has further to run.
picks.risk: A 5x multiple on record margins is what peak-cycle memory looks like; a turn in NAND pricing would cut earnings fast.
